messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: multiple decode/streaming containers on gpu-pool-7 reporting consecutive CUDA OOMs. Auto-quarantine triggered for 3 containers. Pager sent to #oncall. :pager:

rachel_oncall: got the pager. seeing `OOM when allocating tensor` noise in the logs. Is traffic still hitting these nodes? :eyes:

sam_runtime: yes, telemetry shows a spike in average sequence lengths for a small subset of sessions — looks like runaway generation. Kernel logs show fragmentation + failed allocs.

nikhil_sre: node-flap risk. gpu-pool-7 has 2 nodes flapping to Unhealthy in the last 5m. I'm pausing autoscaling to avoid noisy adds causing more OOMs.

maya_platform: routing policy has already moved new requests off pool-7 to fallback pool-3, but existing connections (long-lived streaming) still pinned. We can force-evict sessions if needed.

lee_support: a customer (TICKET-4821) reported partial responses earlier — they lost ~40% of in-flight streaming requests in the timeframe. Confirming impact now.

taylor_cs: flagged the customer and sent a short update: "We're investigating GPU memory errors affecting streaming responses; short-term mitigation in progress."

rachel_oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable token cap enforcement per-request (reject > client-specified max_tokens header), 2) evict long-lived streaming sessions older than X minutes, 3) scale fallback routing to accept new sessions. Which can we do fastest?

sam_runtime: we can flip a runtime flag to enforce `max_tokens` at the socket layer — that will cut off runs that are ignoring header enforcement. Hotpatch path: config roll to runtime-config service -> restart worker loop (no full deploy). I can patch in ~4–6m.

nikhil_sre: in parallel I'll run `kubectl cordon` on the two flapping nodes and drain non-critical pods. If we evict streaming containers they'll either reconnect to fallback pool or failover.

maya_platform: note: evicting will drop active customer streams (some already dropping). If we patch enforcement first, we might avoid mass evictions.

rachel_oncall: prioritize enforcement patch. sam, you have runway; please post the patch cmd and expected artifact.

sam_runtime: applying hotpatch now. patch id: rp-hotpatch-5742. Command:```
# runtime-configctl apply --patch rp-hotpatch-5742 --set enforce_max_tokens=true
# rollout status runtime-config/rp-hotpatch-5742
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: rp-hotpatch-5742 by sam_runtime. Rolling to runtime-nodes in pool-7 then pool-3.

lee_support: checking customer tickets: TICKET-4821 shows 12 aborted streams at 14:02 UTC, correlates with first OOM spike. I'm pinging customer with ETA 20m.

rachel_oncall: after patch, monitor for OOM count drop and memory free signals. Also look for any `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` which could indicate corruption.

sam_runtime: hotpatch completed on pool-7 workers — enforce_max_tokens=true. Observability: per-request token counters now enforced at 1s granularity.

nikhil_sre: OOMs reduced immediately on the patched nodes. Still seeing high mem fragmentation on one node (gpu-7-12). I'm draining it now:```
kubectl drain gpu-7-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

maya_platform: routing shows 88% of new sessions already on fallback pool-3. We'll continue moving traffic until pool-7 healthy.

lee_support: customer update sent: "We applied a mitigation to enforce request token limits which reduced OOMs. Some streams were interrupted; we're continuing mitigation and will follow up."

rachel_oncall: good. need to quantify customer impact and scope: which customers had >N aborted streams, and how many requests were retried/failed?

taylor_cs: working with support to enumerate affected customers. Early list: customer-alpha, customer-bravo, customer-omega (per ticket system). We'll produce a CSV of failures.

sam_runtime: adding telemetry tag `mitigation=rp-hotpatch-5742` to all subsequent traces for rollback tracing. Also logging `evicted_session=true` on any forced disconnects.

nikhil_sre: node gpu-7-12 drained cleanly; pods rescheduled to pool-3. No new OOMs reported from drained node.

maya_platform: we've set a temporary QoS throttle on pool-7 ingress (rate limit per API key) to reduce pressure while pools rebalance. Config: `ingress_qps_per_key=8` until 15:10 UTC.

durga_eng: quick note — we should still investigate why clients were able to generate unbounded sequences despite client max_tokens. Likely a header-parsing fallback bug in the websocket handshake. I'll take lead on a follow-up.

rachel_oncall: assign follow-ups: Durga -> root cause: header parsing + enforcement gap; Sam -> make enforcement permanent in next release; Nikhil -> post-incident node health checks + fragmentation analysis; Maya -> routing safeguards to avoid pinning long-lived streams; Taylor -> customer impact summary + comms.

lee_support: capturing timestamps and counts for TICKET-4821 and related cases. Will add to postmortem.

rachel_oncall: current status: OOM rate down 92% after hotpatch, routing mitigations in place, two nodes drained. Customer impact limited to aborted streams; no data loss reported. Leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: rp-hotpatch-5742 rollout complete — 100% runtime nodes in targeted pools. Audit: deploy-log-5742 available at https://deploys.local/rp-hotpatch-5742

nikhil_sre: scheduling a forensic dump of GPU memory allocator state for gpu-7-11 and gpu-7-13 to understand fragmentation. ETA 24h.

durga_eng: I have a repro harness for header parse fuzzing; will try to replicate clients that send contradictory token headers vs body.

rachel_oncall: thanks all. I'll file the incident and set postmortem owner to durga_eng. Closing pager but keeping oncall watch for 30m.

incident-bot: Pager resolved for incident 2026-03-15-5742003331. Severity: Sev2. Links: https://incidents.local/5742003331
